messages:
Noah Reed: Heads-up: link-checker flagged a bunch of internal anchors after the quickstart restructure. Build failed with `Anchor not found: getting-started-intro referenced from /docs/quickstart.html`.
Noah Reed: full log: ```Error: Could not find anchor #getting-started-intro in /docs/quickstart.html at checkLinks (link-checker/index.js:45)```
Ivy Patel: I think that's from renaming the heading to add clarity — I changed `Getting started: Intro` -> `Getting started: Intro (CLI, SDK)` which changed slug generation. Oops.
Sasha Ivanov: Docusaurus and MkDocs slugify differently for punctuation. Colon -> removed in older slugify, but parentheses lead to dashes in newer versions. That explains the mismatch.
Noah Reed: There are a bunch of pages linking to the old anchor from the sidebar and some migration docs. We should either pin explicit ids on headings or normalize slugs across the site.
Ivy Patel: I'll open a small PR to add explicit heading ids for the major cross-doc anchors and update the outgoing links. Using `{#getting-started-intro}` is safest.
Sasha Ivanov: Also let's add a post-build markdown-link-check step to CI so we catch these before merge. We already run link-check on the compiled site but it's coming too late for quick fixes. Running it in PRs will be helpful.
Noah Reed: Agreed. Can we also add a lint that detects headings that contain colon, parentheses, inline code, emoji, or NBSP and warns if they don't have an explicit `{#id}`? That should catch future regressions.
Sasha Ivanov: I sketched `scripts/ci/check-heading-ids.sh` which parses markdown headings and fails if a heading contains any of `[:()\p{Emoji}\u00A0]` without `{#...}` on the same line. Works in bash + grep + pcre. I'll add it to PR.
Ivy Patel: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1101 — adds explicit ids for the 5 broken anchors, updates links, adds `check-heading-ids.sh` and a docs CI job `docs-lint-heading-ids` that runs in PRs. Also updated CONTRIBUTING with guidance: "If you add punctuation/emoji/code to headings, add an explicit `{#your-id}` to preserve anchors."
docs-bot: label added: docs-review. reviewers requested: Noah Reed, Sasha Ivanov.
Noah Reed: Quick review: LGTM, small nit remove trailing space on one id line. Also can we include a one-line explanation in the PR description about why we prefer explicit ids? New contributors will thank us.
Sasha Ivanov: Added the explanation and a couple of examples in the CONTRIBUTING doc. Also added a unit test that runs markdown-link-check after the build in CI to prevent regressing links.
ci-bot: Running docs CI for PR 1101...
ci-bot: \u2714 build succeeded, \u2714 post-build markdown link-check passed, \u2714 docs-lint-heading-ids passed.
docs-bot: PR #1101 merged by Ivy Patel.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: deploy/docs-staging succeeded (build 451) — site available at https://staging.docs.redwood.ai.
Noah Reed: Verified anchor resolution on staging and spot-checked the sidebar links. All good. Thanks for the quick fix.
Sasha Ivanov: Filed follow-up issue to add a pre-commit hook that runs `scripts/ci/check-heading-ids.sh` locally: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/233.
Ivy Patel: I'll pick the pre-commit hook next sprint and add a short example to the contribution guide. Closing thread once issue is triaged.
